spec_cite: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §7.2 (receivers maintain an RFC 3550 §A.1 extended 64-bit sequence with cycle folding)
description: Sequence wrap: the last datagram of instance 3 carries sequence 0xffffffff; the next carries 0x00000000 — the receiver folds the cycle, extending the sequence to 2^32.
preconditions: Session PLAYING; instance 3 has streamed exactly 2^32 datagrams; timestamps continue on the capture clock.
Both datagrams carry 10 F32LE stereo frames (80 B payload).

steps.note: Last sequence value of the cycle.

assertions: The 32-bit sequence wraps mod 2^32 (0xffffffff -> 0x00000000) — it does NOT trigger a new instance; the instance id and timestamps are unchanged.
The receiver's RFC 3550 A.1 extended sequence folds the cycle: datagram 2's extended sequence is 2^32, not 0; loss/reorder/jitter accounting uses extended values (§7.2).
Timestamp continuity is unaffected by the sequence wrap: 3840000 + 10 = 3840080 (§7.2).
The timestamp itself is a u64 on a 48 kHz clock — ~12.2 million years to wrap; treated as monotonic within the instance (§7.2).
